title: 1958 AHSME Problem 43
statement: \(\overline{AB}\) is the hypotenuse of a right triangle \(ABC.\) Median \(AD=7\) and median \(BE=4.\) The length of \(AB\) is:

solutions.text:
Let \(a=BC,\) \(b=CA,\) and \(c=AB.\) Since the right angle is at \(C,\) \(c^2=a^2+b^2.\) The median formulas give \[ \begin{aligned} 4(7^2) &=a^2+4b^2,\\ 4(4^2) &=4a^2+b^2. \end{aligned} \] Solving yields \(a^2=4\) and \(b^2=48.\) Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} AB=c &=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\\ &=\sqrt{52}=2\sqrt{13}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the legs opposite \(A\) and \(B\) have squared lengths \(u\) and \(v\)
Use the two median formulas together with the Pythagorean relation for the hypotenuse
